newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount Bank Q1 net 62.9 mln shekels.
newsitem.headline: Discount Bank Q1 net 62.9 mln shekels.

text.p: Discount said the 5.7 percent decline in net earnings was due to an 18.6 million shekel charge against its Canadian subsidiary and to inflationary accounting. Without these two items, it said, net would have been 87.9 million shekels, up 44.7 percent on the year.

The seven percent decline in income from financing activities was due to narrower interest margins, which offset higher lending activity, Discount said. The debt provision rose to 15.9 percent in income.
However, income from other activities grew 8.1 percent on the year, which the bank attributed to increased capital market activity.
Annualised net return on equity was 6.2 percent, compared with 6.9 percent a year earlier and 6.0 percent for all of 1996.
Total assets reached 76.6 billion shekels at the end of the quarter, compared with 75.5 billion shekels a year earlier.

Total credit to the public rose 4.6 percent to 41.8 billion shekels, compared with 39.9 billion shekels a year earlier, while deposits from the public rose 4.1 percent to 67.7 billion shekels from 65.0 billion shekels.
